description_full: Allient Inc., together with its subsidiaries, designs, manufactures, and sells precision and specialty-controlled motion components and systems for various industries in the United States, Canada, South America, Europe, and the Asia-Pacific. The company offers various products and solutions, including nano precision positioning systems; servo control systems; motion controllers; digital servo amplifiers and drives; brushless servo; torque; coreless motors, brush motors, integrated motor-drives, gear motors, gearing, incremental and absolute optical encoders, and active electronic and passive magnetic filters for power quality and harmonic issues; industrial safety rated input/output modules; universal industrial communications gateways; and light-weighting technologies and other controlled motion-related products. It sells its products in industrial, vehicle, medical, and aerospace and defense markets through direct sales force, authorized manufacturers' representatives, and distributors. The company was formerly known as Allied Motion Technologies Inc. and changed its name to Allient Inc. in August 2023. Allient Inc. was founded in 1939 and is headquartered in Williamsville, New York.

financial_summary: Allient Inc. is a small-cap technology business with a $1.3B market cap on $554M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +9% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 8% against a 10% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 30%.

The business throws off $50M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.57× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.0× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and interest coverage runs at 3.3×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.2%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.3× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
